title: Investigating potential molecular mechanisms linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: A network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation study.
authors: Yang, Bin; Wang, Xiangjin; Zhuo, Li; Chen, Yutong; He, Qiansong
one_liner_zh: 该研究用网络毒理学、分子对接和MD模拟探讨污染物6PPD-Q与椎间盘退变的关联，核心是化合物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). ADMET toxicological predictions indicated high model-predicted probabilities for SR-MMP and SR-ARE activation. Through multidimensional database integration, 59 common targets potentially associated with 6PPD-Q and IVDD were identified. Protein-protein interaction network analysis further identified five hub genes: PTGS2, MMP2, SMAD3, RELA, and GSK3B. Functional enrichment analysis suggested that these targets were mainly involved in AGE-RAGE, PI3K-Akt, MAPK, TNF, and IL-17 signaling pathways, collectively implicating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Molecular docking showed favorable predicted binding between 6PPD-Q and the five hub proteins, with RELA exhibiting the most favorable docking score (-8.82 kcal/mol). A subsequent 100-ns MD simulation of the 6PPD-Q-RELA complex showed relatively stable RMSD, Rg, and SASA profiles and a concentrated low-energy conformational basin, supporting its dynamic stability under the simulated conditions. Collectively, these computational findings suggest potential molecular links between 6PPD-Q exposure and IVDD and provide hypotheses for subsequent experimental validation.
abstract_zh: 作为一种源自轮胎橡胶的新兴污染物，6PPD-醌（6PPD-Q）因广泛的环境暴露已引发公众健康关注；然而，其对无血管组织（如椎间盘）的潜在毒理学效应仍不清楚。本研究整合了网络毒理学、分子对接和分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟，以探讨6PPD-Q暴露与椎间盘退变（intervertebral disc degeneration, IVDD）之间的潜在机制。ADMET毒理学预测显示，SR-MMP和SR-ARE激活的模型预测概率较高。通过多维数据库整合，识别出59个可能与6PPD-Q和IVDD相关的共同靶点。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络分析进一步确定了五个枢纽基因：PTGS2、MMP2、SMAD3、RELA和GSK3B。功能富集分析提示，这些靶点主要涉及AGE-RAGE、PI3K-Akt、MAPK、TNF和IL-17信号通路，共同涉及氧化应激、炎症和凋亡。分子对接显示6PPD-Q与五个枢纽蛋白之间具有有利的预测结合，其中RELA表现出最优的对接得分（-8.82 kcal/mol）。随后对6PPD-Q-RELA复合物进行的100纳秒MD模拟显示，RMSD、Rg和SASA曲线相对稳定，并呈现集中的低能构象盆地，支持其在模拟条件下的动态稳定性。综合来看，这些计算发现提示6PPD-Q暴露与IVDD之间存在潜在的分子关联，并为后续实验验证提供了假设。
